subject: Mathematics
title: Application of Derivatives
summary: Derivatives give rates of change, slopes of tangents and normals, and tell where a function increases, decreases, or has maxima and minima.
First-derivative test (sign change of f′) and second-derivative test (sign of f″) locate local extrema; absolute extrema on [a, b] are among critical points and end points.
Rolle's theorem and the mean value theorem link average and instantaneous rates. Optimisation word problems — areas, volumes, distances — are standard JEE questions.

formulas.name: Rate of change
formulas.when: Related rates (area, volume changing with time).

formulas.name: Tangent and normal
formulas.formula: tangent: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), m = f′(x₁);  normal: y − y₁ = −(1/m)(x − x₁)

formulas.name: Increasing / decreasing
formulas.formula: f′(x) > 0 ⇒ strictly increasing;  f′(x) < 0 ⇒ strictly decreasing
formulas.note: f′ can be 0 at isolated points and f still increasing (x³ at 0).

formulas.name: Critical points
formulas.formula: f′(c) = 0 or f′(c) does not exist

formulas.name: First-derivative test
formulas.formula: f′ changes + to − ⇒ local maximum;  − to + ⇒ local minimum;  no change ⇒ neither (point of inflection)

formulas.name: Second-derivative test
formulas.formula: f′(c) = 0 and f″(c) < 0 ⇒ local max;  f″(c) > 0 ⇒ local min;  f″(c) = 0 ⇒ test fails

formulas.name: Absolute extrema on [a, b]
formulas.formula: compare f at all critical points in (a, b) and at a, b
formulas.when: Global max/min on a closed interval.

formulas.name: Rolle's theorem
formulas.formula: f continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), f(a) = f(b) ⇒ ∃ c ∈ (a, b): f′(c) = 0

formulas.name: Lagrange's mean value theorem
formulas.formula: f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for some c ∈ (a, b)

formulas.name: Standard optimisation results
formulas.formula: fixed perimeter → square has max area;  fixed surface area → cube (or sphere) has max volume;  cylinder of max volume in a sphere: h = 2R/√3

formulas.name: Angle between curves
formulas.formula: tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| using slopes of tangents at the intersection;  orthogonal if m₁m₂ = −1

examples.title: Local extrema
examples.problem: Find the local maximum and minimum values of f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5.

examples.title: Related rates
examples.problem: A sphere's radius grows at 0.1 cm/s. How fast is the volume growing when r = 5 cm?

examples.title: Maximum area
examples.problem: Maximum area of a rectangle with perimeter 20?

examples.title: Mean value theorem
examples.problem: Find c for f(x) = x² on [1, 3].

topics.title: Monotonicity and inequalities
topics.explain: To prove f(x) > g(x) for x > 0, show h = f − g has h(0) = 0 and h′ > 0. Example: eˣ > 1 + x for x ≠ 0.

topics.title: Points of inflection
topics.explain: Where f″ changes sign (concavity changes). f is concave up where f″ > 0 and concave down where f″ < 0.

topics.title: Optimisation steps
topics.explain: Write the quantity to optimise in one variable using the constraint, find critical points, test them, and check endpoints/domain restrictions.

topics.title: Shortest distance problems
topics.explain: Minimise the square of the distance instead of the distance — same minimiser, easier algebra.

topics.title: Tangents from an external point
topics.explain: Write the tangent at a general point (t, f(t)) and make it pass through the given point; solve for t.

ratta: Fixed perimeter → square;  fixed surface → cube.
